$comment: Allowlist for run_lxc_command. Matching is on argv prefix; argv comes from whitespace-splitting `command`, or verbatim from the `args` array. No shell is ever invoked, so metacharacters are inert — the `command` path still rejects them for clarity, the `args` path does not, which is what it is for. deny_always wins over any allow rule.

mutating_scoped.$comment: Allowed only with working_dir equal to the registered startup working dir, so an agent can manage the app it deployed but nothing else.

mutating_service.$comment: Service control, allowed anywhere in the guest (no working-dir gate). write_lxc_file + rerun_startup already executes an arbitrary root script in this same guest, so denying these never constrained capability — only convenience, at the cost of pushing every mutation through a slower and less auditable redeploy. Unit creation, enablement and package installation still belong in the startup script, where they are recorded and re-runnable.

deny_always.$comment: Never allowed regardless of other rules.

rationale.docker compose down: Removes containers and networks; restart/stop cover every legitimate need without deletion.
rationale.apt/apt-get/dpkg: Package changes belong in the startup script where they are recorded and re-runnable, not in ad-hoc exec.
rationale.shells and interpreters: Would make the allowlist a formality.
rationale.curl with output flags / wget: curl is allowed for probing only; writing fetched bytes to disk is arbitrary code delivery. Flag matching is on exact tokens and bundled short-flag clusters (-sSo is denied), never on a flag's VALUE — -HConnection:Upgrade is a header, not an output flag.
rationale.systemctl restart/reload: NOT denied — see mutating_service. Restarting a unit the guest already has is allowed directly, because rerun_startup can already do it with more steps and less audit.
